This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: The user is building "Vibe Voyager" — an interactive space exploration game teaching vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. It will be hosted at [REDACTED_DOMAIN] on Vercel free tier. The user has a lecture in ~1 week (from 2026-03-07). They chose "subagent-driven development" to execute a 9-phase, 39-task implementation plan with parallel agent teams. This session continued from a previous session that ran out of context, picking up at Phase 3 (partially complete) and driving through Phases 3, 4, and 5 to completion. The user approved compacting before Phase 6+7 (the biggest content wave). User preferences: - **Do NOT commit** CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md, docs/, .claude/, .playwright-mcp/ to git — all gitignored - Main thread handles all git commits (subagents can't run bash) - Commit after each agent's work, not batched - Update BUILD_LOG.md after each phase and before every compaction 2. Key Technical Concepts: - **Next.js 15.5.12** with App Router, TypeScript, React 19 - **Tailwind CSS v4** — CSS-first config with `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` directive, NO tailwind.config.js - **Motion** package (v12) — import from `motion/react`, NOT `framer-motion` - **Motion Variants strict types**: Must use `as const` on variant objects or `type: 'spring' as const` to satisfy TypeScript literal type requirements - **Next.js 15 async params**: Route `params` is a Promise — use `React.use(params)` in client components - **Howler.js** for audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites) - **HTML5 Canvas** for star map rendering - **localStorage** for all game state (no backend, no database, no auth) - **clsx** for className composition (NOT `cn`) - **Subagent-driven development** — fresh agent per task, parallel within phases, zero file overlap - **Mini-game uniform API**: All 5 mini-games accept `onComplete(score: number)` where score is 0-100 - **Glassmorphism pattern**: `bg-glass backdrop-blur-md border border-glass-border rounded-xl` - **AnimatePresence** with `mode="wait"` for page/phase transitions 3. Files and Code Sections: **Phase 3 Files (committed this session):** - `app/page.tsx` — Title screen with animated starfield and menu. Fixed Motion Variants type error: ```typescript const container = { hidden: { opacity: 0 }, show: { opacity: 1, transition: { staggerChildren: 0.18, delayChildren: 0.4 }, }, } as const const item = { hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 24 }, show: { opacity: 1, y: 0, transition: { type: 'spring' as const, stiffness: 80, damping: 16 }, }, } ``` - `app/create/page.tsx` (366 lines) — 3-step character creation: callsign input, ship selection (Spark/Architect/Sentinel with inline SVGs), Star Wars text crawl with CSS perspective animation, spring transitions between steps - `app/cockpit/page.tsx` (285 lines) — Cockpit HUD: player identity/rank badge, 4-stat gauge grid, crew roster circles, mission progress bar with act breakdown, first-visit ARIA welcome overlay with TypewriterText - `app/starmap/page.tsx` (20 lines) — Thin wrapper redirecting to `/` if no save, renders StarMap component - `components/game/StarMap.tsx` (500 lines) — Full Canvas-based galaxy map: 3-layer parallax stars, 8 planets with 4 status states (locked/available/in_progress/completed), orbital progress rings, connection lines between planets, Academy diamond shape, click navigation with tooltips, hover cursor changes, DPR-aware rendering - `components/game/NavBar.tsx` (158 lines) — Fixed bottom navigation: 5 items (Map/Cockpit/Crew/Items/Academy) with inline SVG icons + AudioToggle. Hidden on `/` and `/create` via HIDDEN_ROUTES array - `app/layout.tsx` — Updated to include AudioProvider wrapper and NavBar, added `pb-20` for bottom nav clearance: ```tsx
{children}
 ``` **Phase 4 Files:** - `components/game/DialogueSystem.tsx` (334 lines) — Full-screen overlay NPC conversation engine: speaker portrait lookup from crew data, TypewriterText animation, branching choice buttons with correct/incorrect feedback (green/red flash), score tracking, quiz summary screen, `onComplete(score: 0-100)` - `components/game/MissionBriefing.tsx` — Mission title, ARIA dialogue via TypewriterText, challenge type badge, "Begin Mission" button - `components/game/LearningPhase.tsx` — Scrollable content rendering LearningBlock types: text (with optional highlight border), code (monospace preformatted), stat (terracotta callout), image (placeholder) - `components/game/MissionDebrief.tsx` — Score percentage display, star rating (3/2/1 stars), animated stat gains, item/crew reward cards, next/return buttons - `app/planets/[planetId]/page.tsx` — Planet landing page: planet header with color tinting, mission list as GlassPanel cards with status indicators (locked/available/in_progress/completed), mission click navigation. Uses `React.use(params)` for Next.js 15 async params. - `app/planets/[planetId]/mission/[missionId]/page.tsx` (900 lines total for framework) — Mission flow with 4-phase state machine: briefing → learning → challenge (placeholder with mock complete button, score 80) → debrief. Uses AnimatePresence between phases. Calls `completeMission()` from useGame context on challenge complete. - `app/inventory/page.tsx` — Grid of 7 item cards: acquired items show icon, name, real-world tool, description, category badge with color; unacquired show "???" with opacity-40 - `app/crew/page.tsx` — Grid of 5 crew member cards: recruited show portrait circle, name, role, agent phase badge, description, italic quote; unrecruited show "?" with location hint derived from recruitedAt **Phase 5 Files:** - `components/games/PromptDuel.tsx` (157 lines) — Write prompts for scenarios, case-insensitive keyword scoring, results showing found/missed concepts - `components/games/Architect.tsx` (446 lines) — Drag-and-drop diagram builder: HTML DnD API for desktop, tap-to-select for mobile, slot highlighting (green=correct, red=wrong) - `components/games/Connect.tsx` (427 lines) — SVG bezier wiring puzzle: click source then target to connect, curved lines, correct/incorrect feedback on check - `components/games/Debug.tsx` (283 lines) — Click code lines to find bugs: line selection with terracotta highlight, false-positive-aware scoring formula: `Math.max(0, ((correct - falsePositives) / bugLines.length) * 100)` - `components/games/Command.tsx` (405 lines) — Agent-to-task assignment: Motion drag with hit-testing for desktop, tap-to-select for mobile, agent swapping logic, exported types (TaskItem, AgentItem, CommandProps) **Key Reference Files (read but not modified):** - `lib/types.ts` (103 lines) — All TypeScript interfaces: PlayerStats, GameState, Mission, MissionContent, DialogueNode, DialogueChoice, LearningBlock, ChallengeData, PlanetId, ShipType, Rank, etc. - `lib/game-context.tsx` (74 lines) — React context: GameProvider, useGame hook with startNewGame, resetGame, completeMission, rank, totalStats, completedMissions - `lib/game-state.ts` (145 lines) — State functions: createNewGame, saveGame, loadGame, completeMission, getRank, getTotalStats, getPlanetStatus, isPlanetComplete - `lib/data/planets.ts` — 8 planets with positions, prerequisites, colors, TOTAL_MISSIONS=34, MISSION_COUNTS lookup - `lib/data/missions.ts` — 34 mission stubs with metadata (empty content arrays to be filled in Phase 6) - `lib/data/crew.ts` — 5 crew members: ARIA, Scout, Archie, Exec, Mirror with CrewMemberDef type (id, name, role, agentPhase, color, quote, recruitedAt) - `components/ui/index.ts` — Barrel exports: GlassPanel, StarfieldBackground, TypewriterText, StatGauge, XPBar, Button **Build Tracking Files (updated):** - `BUILD_LOG.md` — Updated with Phase 3, 4, 5 completion data, running notes, agent teams log - Fixed by adding `as const` to the container object and `type: 'spring' as const` to the item variant's transition. This is a common gotcha when using Motion v12's strict types — it requires literal types, not plain strings. - **Stale memory files**: `memory/tech-stack.md` still referenced "Next.js 14" and "Framer Motion". # Planet-by-Planet Content Mapping

## ACT 1 — "The Solo Pilot"

### Vibe World (4 missions)
1. "First Words" — What is vibe coding (IBM, Replit, Wikipedia, Google Cloud) → Dialogue
2. "See It, Say It, Run It" — First vibe creation (Slide 2, Beginner Guide) → Prompt Duel
3. "The Prototype Sprint" — Build fast (arXiv: Vibe Coding in Practice) → Timed challenge
4. "Traditional vs. Vibe" — Both paradigms (arXiv: GenAI & Software Dev) → Dialogue/debate

### Debt Asteroid Belt (4 missions)
1. "The Fragile Ship" — Tech debt (Slide 9, Tabnine) → Debug
2. "The Quality Crisis" — 2026 data: 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x XSS, 4x code cloning (CodeRabbit, Black Duck) → Debug real vuln types
3. "Your Career in the AI Era" — Junior dev employment drops 9-10%, AI unlocks new domains (Harvard, Stack Overflow) → Career counselor dialogue
4. "The Case for Expertise" — Vibe alone isn't enough, Karpathy quote, transition to agentic engineering → Dialogue quiz, unlocks Act 2

## ACT 2 — "First Contact"

### MCP Station (5 missions)
1. "The N×M Problem" — Integration bottleneck (Slide 4) → Visual puzzle
2. "USB-C for AI" — MCP: 97M downloads, Linux Foundation (Slide 5, Anthropic, IBM, Context Studios) → Connect puzzle
3. "Protocol vs. Wrappers" — MCP 1.0 targeting June 2026 (Slide 6) → Dialogue quiz
4. "Docking Sequence" — Hands-on MCP config (Anthropic docs) → Architect
5. "The Babel Problem" — A2A protocol: agents can use tools but can't talk to each other (Google A2A, Linux Foundation) → Connect puzzle

### Agent Academy (5 missions)
1. "The Cognitive Loop" — Agent anatomy (Slide 3) → Architect, recruits Scout
2. "Perception Training" — How agents see (arXiv) → Sorting mini-game
3. "Planning & Reasoning" — Chain of thought (arXiv, Deep Agent article) → Architect tree, recruits Archie
4. "Tool Calling" — How agents act (Akka, ACI) → Connect puzzle
5. "Self-Healing" — Reflect loop (Slide 3 callout) → Debug scenarios, recruits Exec

### Framework Nebula (5 missions)
1. "Three Schools of Thought" — LangGraph vs CrewAI vs AutoGen (Slide 8, DataCamp) → NPC dialogues
2. "The Official Armories" — Vendor SDKs: Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK → Comparison + Architect
3. "The Right Tool" — When to use what: frameworks vs SDKs vs custom → Command matching
4. "Build a Crew" — CrewAI concepts (repos) → Architect fill-in-blank
5. "Agent Cards" — A2A capability discovery, AGENTS.md config → Architect: build Agent Card JSON

## ACT 3 — "Fleet Commander"

### Orchestration Citadel (4 missions)
1. "Society of Agents" — Multi-agent pipeline (Slide 7) → Architect
2. "The A2A Network" — A2A deep dive: capability discovery, task delegation, 72% enterprise adoption → Connect routing
3. "Message Passing" — Agent communication (arXiv, Devin) → Connect puzzle
4. "Delegation" — 87% of Fortune 500 use AI tools → Command triage

### Security Fortress (4 missions)
1. "The Safety Net" — HITL (Slide 10, Galileo) → Architect flowchart, recruits Mirror
2. "Local Defenses" — Local LLMs (Slide 11) → Dialogue quiz
3. "Threat Scan" — Security in agents (Auto Fixer, CWE-95, Black Duck 2026) → Debug
4. "The Legal Frontier" — AI copyright, licensing, disclosure rules (U.S. Copyright Office, Red Hat) → Dialogue quiz

### Production Worlds (3 missions)
1. "Moon Alpha: QE" — Self-healing tests (Slide 12, SWE-bench) → Command
2. "Moon Beta: Enterprise" — Real-world cases (Slide 13, healthcare/BFSI/supply) → Dialogue
3. "Final Mission: Deployment Playbook" — Capstone (Slides 14-15) → Multi-step Architect

## EPILOGUE — "The Academy" (10 Sections)

### Section 1: AI-Powered IDEs & Editors
**GUI IDEs:** Cursor, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot
**Terminal Agents:** Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider
**VS Code Extensions:** Cline, Roo Code, Continue
**Other Notable:** JetBrains AI, Amazon Q, Tabnine, Sourcegraph Cody

### Section 2: AI Code Review & Quality
CodeRabbit, Greptile, Qodo, Ellipsis, Cursor BugBot

### Section 3: No-Code / Low-Code Builders
Replit, Bolt.new, Lovable, v0 by Vercel

### Section 4: Agent SDKs & Protocols
Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, MCP (97M downloads, 1.0 spec), A2A (150+ partners), AGENTS.md (60k+ projects)

### Section 5: Claude Code Deep Dive
Installation, CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, agent teams, keybindings, MCP servers, best practices cycle

### Section 6: Agentic Development Best Practices
Subagent-driven dev, parallelization, AI code review, TDD with agents, memory management, security/HITL, prompt engineering, tech debt

### Section 7: MCP Workshop
What/why, setting up servers (stdio/HTTP), connecting tools, building your own server, enterprise governance

### Section 8: Resource Library
All 57+ sources from sources.md, organized by topic

### Section 9: How This Was Built
Meta case study from BUILD_LOG.md

### Section 10: Career Paths
AI-Native Developer, AI Full-Stack Developer, Prompt Engineer, Agentic Engineer — mapping game skills to real roles

- Agent SDKs & protocols content → Academy Section 4
- Claude Code deep dive tutorials → Academy Section 5
- Agentic best practices guide → Academy Section 6
- MCP setup walkthrough → Academy Section 7 + MCP Station
- Career paths research → Academy Section 10
- Mini-game interactive content → all challenges
- NPC dialogue scripts → all planets
- Audio assets → global
- Planet/character SVG illustrations → global

export type StatName = 'vibe' | 'architecture' | 'protocol' | 'command'

export interface PlayerStats {
  vibe: number
  architecture: number
  protocol: number
  command: number
}

export type Rank = 'Cadet' | 'Navigator' | 'Commander' | 'Admiral'
export type ShipType = 'spark' | 'architect' | 'sentinel'

export interface CrewMember {
  id: string
  name: string
  role: string
  description: string
  recruitedAt: string
  portrait: string
}

export interface InventoryItem {
  id: string
  name: string
  realWorldTool: string
  description: string
  icon: string
  acquiredAt: string
}

export type MissionStatus = 'locked' | 'available' | 'in_progress' | 'completed'

export interface MissionProgress {
  missionId: string
  status: MissionStatus
  score?: number
  completedAt?: string
}

export type ChallengeType = 'prompt-duel' | 'architect' | 'connect' | 'debug' | 'command' | 'dialogue'

export interface Mission {
  id: string
  planetId: PlanetId
  title: string
  subtitle: string
  description: string
  challengeType: ChallengeType
  statRewards: Partial<PlayerStats>
  itemReward?: string
  crewReward?: string
  order: number
  content: MissionContent
}

export interface MissionContent {
  briefing: DialogueNode[]
  learning: LearningBlock[]
  challenge: ChallengeData
  debrief: DialogueNode[]
}

export interface DialogueNode {
  speaker: string
  text: string
  choices?: DialogueChoice[]
}

export interface DialogueChoice {
  text: string
  correct?: boolean
  response?: string
  nextNodeIndex?: number
}

export interface LearningBlock {
  type: 'text' | 'code' | 'stat' | 'image'
  content: string
  highlight?: boolean
}

export interface ChallengeData {
  type: ChallengeType
  instructions: string
  data: Record<string, unknown>
  passingScore: number
}

export type PlanetId = 'vibe-world' | 'debt-belt' | 'mcp-station' | 'agent-academy' | 'framework-nebula' | 'orchestration-citadel' | 'security-fortress' | 'production-worlds'
export type PlanetStatus = 'locked' | 'available' | 'in_progress' | 'completed'

export interface GameState {
  callsign: string
  ship: ShipType
  stats: PlayerStats
  crew: string[]
  inventory: string[]
  missionProgress: Record<string, MissionProgress>
  currentPlanet?: PlanetId
  currentMission?: string
  createdAt: string
  lastPlayedAt: string
}

## Phase 6: Planet Content (Parallel — 8 agents, one per planet)

> Each planet is completely independent. Dispatch all 8 simultaneously.
> Dependency: Phase 5 must be complete (mini-games available for challenges).
> Content source: `notebooklm-content/sources.md`, design doc Section 6, gap analysis doc.

Each agent creates mission content for one planet: dialogue trees, learning blocks, and challenge data. All content lives in `lib/data/missions/[planetId].ts`.

### Task 6.1: Vibe World Content (4 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/vibe-world.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "First Words" — Dialogue quiz. ARIA explains vibe coding. Quiz on definitions.
2. "See It, Say It, Run It" — Prompt Duel. Write a prompt to build a simple app.
3. "The Prototype Sprint" — Timed Prompt Duel. Write prompts under time pressure.
4. "Traditional vs. Vibe" — Dialogue debate. Compare paradigms, answer questions.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Vibe per mission
**Item reward:** Ship Voice Module (mission 1)
**Sources:** IBM vibe coding article, Replit guide, Karpathy tweet, arXiv papers

### Task 6.2: Debt Asteroid Belt Content (4 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/debt-belt.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "The Fragile Ship" — Debug. Find 5 tech debt problems in code.
2. "The Quality Crisis" — Debug. Real vulnerability types (XSS, insecure refs). Stats: 1.75x bugs, 2.74x XSS.
3. "Your Career in the AI Era" — Dialogue. Career counselor NPC discusses junior dev impact.
4. "The Case for Expertise" — Dialogue quiz. Karpathy's evolution quote. Unlocks Act 2.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Vibe, +1 Architecture
**Sources:** CodeRabbit report, Black Duck OSSRA 2026, Harvard study, Karpathy quote

### Task 6.3: MCP Station Content (5 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/mcp-station.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "The N×M Problem" — Architect. Arrange integration complexity diagram.
2. "USB-C for AI" — Connect. Wire MCP connections (client → server → tools).
3. "Protocol vs. Wrappers" — Dialogue quiz. MCP vs direct API wrappers.
4. "Docking Sequence" — Architect. Build MCP config JSON.
5. "The Babel Problem" — Connect. Wire agents to agents via A2A.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Protocol per mission
**Item reward:** Context Adapter (mission 2)
**Sources:** Anthropic MCP docs, Google A2A blog, Linux Foundation

### Task 6.4: Agent Academy Content (5 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/agent-academy.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "The Cognitive Loop" — Architect. Build the Perceive→Plan→Act→Reflect cycle. Recruits Scout.
2. "Perception Training" — Command. Sort inputs by perception type.
3. "Planning & Reasoning" — Architect. Build a chain-of-thought tree. Recruits Archie.
4. "Tool Calling" — Connect. Wire agent to tools.
5. "Self-Healing" — Debug. Fix agent error recovery scenarios. Recruits Exec.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Architecture per mission
**Item reward:** Agent Blueprint (mission 1)
**Crew rewards:** Scout (M1), Archie (M3), Exec (M5)

### Task 6.5: Framework Nebula Content (5 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/framework-nebula.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "Three Schools of Thought" — Dialogue. Compare LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen.
2. "The Official Armories" — Dialogue + Architect. Compare Claude SDK, OpenAI SDK, Google ADK.
3. "The Right Tool" — Command. Match frameworks to use cases.
4. "Build a Crew" — Architect. Arrange CrewAI components.
5. "Agent Cards" — Architect. Build an A2A Agent Card JSON.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Architecture, +1 Protocol
**Sources:** DataCamp comparison, SDK docs, A2A protocol docs, AGENTS.md spec

### Task 6.6: Orchestration Citadel Content (4 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/orchestration-citadel.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "Society of Agents" — Architect. Build multi-agent pipeline.
2. "The A2A Network" — Connect. Route messages between agents via Agent Cards.
3. "Message Passing" — Connect. Wire agent communication patterns.
4. "Delegation" — Command. Triage tasks to appropriate agents.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Command per mission
**Item reward:** Fleet Comm Array (mission 1)

### Task 6.7: Security Fortress Content (4 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/security-fortress.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "The Safety Net" — Architect. Build HITL flowchart. Recruits Mirror.
2. "Local Defenses" — Dialogue quiz. When and why to use local LLMs.
3. "Threat Scan" — Debug. Find security vulnerabilities in agent code.
4. "The Legal Frontier" — Dialogue quiz. Mirror raises copyright/licensing concerns.

**Stat rewards:** +1-2 Command, +1 Protocol
**Item rewards:** Security Shield (M1), Local Core (M2)
**Crew reward:** Mirror (M1)

### Task 6.8: Production Worlds Content (3 missions)

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/data/missions/production-worlds.ts`

**Missions:**
1. "Moon Alpha: Quality Engineering" — Command. Assign agents to testing tasks.
2. "Moon Beta: The Enterprise" — Dialogue quiz. Real-world deployment cases.
3. "Final Mission: Deployment Playbook" — Multi-step Architect. Build complete deployment architecture.

**Stat rewards:** +2 Command per mission (capstone)
**Item reward:** Skill Chips (mission 3)

Now I have a complete picture. Let me understand what each mini-game needs as challenge data:

1. **PromptDuel** — `{ scenario: string, requiredConcepts: string[] }`
2. **Architect** — `{ nodes: ArchNode[], slots: ArchSlot[] }` where `ArchNode = { id, label }`, `ArchSlot = { id, label, correctNodeId }`
3. **Connect** — `{ sources: string[], targets: string[], correctPairs: [number, number][] }`
4. **Debug** — `{ code: string, bugLines: number[], explanations: Record<number, string> }`


5. **Command** — `{ tasks: TaskItem[], agents: AgentItem[], correctAssignments: Record<string, string> }` where `TaskItem = { id, label, description }`, `AgentItem = { id, label, specialty }`
6. **Dialogue** — Already built into DialogueSystem, uses `briefing: DialogueNode[]` with choices

The mission page has a placeholder challenge phase right now, so content agents need to create per-planet content files in `lib/data/missions/[planetId].ts` that export the challenge data for each game type.

Looking at the current setup, `missions.ts` has the content inline but the stubs are empty. I'm deciding between putting content in separate files versus keeping it all in one place — the plan calls for separate files, so I'll go with that approach and wire them up to the mission definitions. The `makeMission` helper currently creates empty content objects with default values, so I need to modify how those get populated.

The cleanest way forward is to have each planet file export content keyed by mission ID, then create a function that merges that content into the missions. I also need to check what the DialogueSystem expects for the challenge phase, since that's currently just a placeholder on the mission page. So I'm looking at two main pieces of work: building out the planet content files and wiring up the actual challenge components.

Actually, the wiring should probably happen first—I need to import all the mini-game components and DialogueSystem, then switch on the mission's challengeType to render the right component with the challenge data as props. This is critical to get working before adding content, otherwise the games won't actually function when the content is added.

Now I'm thinking through what data structure each mini-game needs. PromptDuel takes a scenario and required concepts, Architect needs nodes and slots, Connect requires sources, targets, and correct pairs, Debug needs code with bug line numbers and explanations, and Command takes tasks, agents, and correct assignments. For the dialogue challenge type, it looks like it uses the briefing DialogueNode array instead of separate challenge data.

Let me figure out the DialogueSystem component interface. From what I remember about it, it handles speaker portraits from crew data, animates text with a typewriter effect, shows branching choices with visual feedback for correct and incorrect answers, tracks the quiz score, and displays a summary screen before calling onComplete with the final score.

- Debrief: ARIA congratulates, mentions the Ship Voice Module reward (2 nodes)

- Topic: Writing your first vibe-coding prompt

- Challenge data shape for prompt-duel: `{ scenario: string, requiredConcepts: string[] }` — scenario asks player to write a prompt to build a simple todo app. requiredConcepts: keywords like "todo", "add", "delete", "list", "complete" (5-7 concepts, case-insensitive matched)
- Debrief: ARIA reviews what makes good prompts (2 nodes)

- Do NOT use \! in any strings (causes TS1127)
- Make content genuinely educational about vibe coding concepts

# How This Was Built: A Claude Code Case Study

> This document tracks the entire process of building [REDACTED_DOMAIN] using Claude Code with agent teams, plugins, and skills. It serves as both a behind-the-scenes look and living proof of the agentic development practices taught on the platform.

## Build Metadata
- **Start Date:** 2026-03-07
- **Target:** Full game experience in ~1 week
- **Stack:** Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Canvas, Howler.js
- **Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
- **Primary Tool:** Claude Code (Opus 4.6)

## Phase 1: Brainstorming & Design
- **Approach:** Used `superpowers:brainstorming` skill for structured design exploration
- **Decisions made through dialogue:**
  - Audience: Mixed levels (beginner to advanced)
  - Format: Full game experience (not just a course with game skin)
  - Narrative: Space exploration — Solo Pilot → First Contact → Fleet Commander → Academy
  - Visual style: Clean minimalist sci-fi (glassmorphism, Framer Motion, SVG)
  - Audio: Full soundscape (ambient + UI SFX)
  - Tech: Next.js + HTML5 Canvas (no game engine — agents parallelize React better)
  - Academy: Hybrid format (space aesthetic, real-world content)
- **Content base:** NotebookLM deep research — 15-slide PDF, mind map, infographic, 57+ curated sources, beginner's guide doc, key findings spreadsheet
